problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a collection of fragile cargo units into standardized transport pods. The cargo units are as follows:

* Component Alpha: mass 33 units
* Component Beta: mass 66 units
* Component Gamma: mass 32 units
* Component Delta: mass 56 units
* Component Epsilon: mass 35 units
* Component Zeta: mass 46 units
* Component Eta: mass 42 units
* Component Theta: mass 50 units
* Component Iota: mass 41 units
* Component Kappa: mass 37 units
* Component Lambda: mass 41 units
* Component Mu: mass 53 units
* Component Nu: mass 31 units
* Component Xi: mass 44 units
* Component Omicron: mass 32 units
* Component Pi: mass 30 units
* Component Rho: mass 54 units
* Component Sigma: mass 64 units
* Component Tau: mass 30 units
* Component Upsilon: mass 38 units
* Component Phi: mass 37 units
* Component Chi: mass 68 units

Each transport pod possesses a maximum safe load capacity of 100 mass units. The coordinator must assign every cargo unit to precisely one pod, ensuring the aggregate mass within any given pod does not surpass its load limit. The objective is to accomplish this allocation while employing the minimal possible number of pods.
